annotation.kind: direct formalization of Lemma 3.10 and equations (3.8)-(3.9)

assumptions: The number of rounding errors is positive.
The finite probability law has nonnegative masses summing to one.
The unit-roundoff and bias-roundoff bounds are nonnegative.
For alpha_k=delta_k-beta_k, |alpha_k| is bounded by the unit roundoff and |beta_k| is bounded by the bias roundoff.
Against every finite test function determined by preceding alpha errors, delta_k and beta_k have the same conditional mean.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P17 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P17 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p17_t3_centered_product_decomposition {n : Nat} {Omega : Type*} [Fintype Omega] (run : P17Lemma310Run n Omega) : centered mean independence of alpha and, for every suffix and outcome, the power-set product decomposition (3.8) and gamma-difference remainder bound (3.9)
formal_statement.plain_language: The centered errors alpha_k=delta_k-beta_k are mean independent, and every suffix product of the original errors splits into the centered suffix product plus the explicit power-set remainder bounded in equation (3.9).

informal_proof: Use the conditional-mean identity and linearity of finite expectation to center alpha. Apply the power-set expansion of Lemma 3.9 to each suffix. Bound every mixed monomial using |alpha_k|<=u_p and |beta_k|<=u_(p+r), group subsets by cardinality, and use the binomial theorem to obtain the difference of gamma terms.
informal_statement: Lemma 3.10: the centered limited-precision stochastic-rounding errors are mean independent and satisfy the product decomposition (3.8) with the remainder bound (3.9).
paper_version: published journal version; SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 47(5), 2025, pages B1227-B1249

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The nearby declarations provide only elementary finite-expectation algebra. Neither baseline contains the history-conditioned centering together with the paper's explicit mixed-monomial decomposition and gamma-difference bound.

tier_rationale: The target requires a history-conditioned finite-expectation argument, a suffix-indexed power-set product expansion, and a sharp mixed-monomial bound collected by subset cardinality. NumStability has no corresponding combined result, and its nearby expectation identities are routine support that does not materially shorten the proof.
